Name: Active Window Controls
Author: Harbor
Description: Double-click the active app title in the Dock to maximize it. Right-click for window actions.
Instructions:
Install and make sure the Active window piece is enabled in Dock controls.
Double-click the active app title in the top Dock to maximize or restore its window.
Right-click that title for minimize, close, always-on-top, and app-specific plugin actions.

Name: Always on Top
Author: Harbor
Description: Keep chosen apps above other windows, even while you work in another app.
Instructions:
Install, then enter the apps that should stay above other windows. The default example matches notepad.exe.
Use one executable name per line, such as Discord.exe. Optional title patterns narrow the match.
Click Apply settings and open a matching app. Pause or uninstall the plugin to restore normal stacking.

Options.Label: Apps, one pattern per line (* matches any text)
Excluded apps or titles, one pattern per line

Name: App Collection
Author: Harbor
Description: Keep app, folder and website shortcuts behind a small movable control.
Instructions:
Install, then open Harbor's Apps screen to find the small Apps control. Click it to expand the tool; click away or press Esc to collapse.
In Shortcuts, use one Label | path per line. Example: Calculator | calc.exe or Website | https://example.com.
Click Apply settings. Click a named button in the widget to open its app, folder, or website.
Right-click the control for Visibility, Position and Appearance. Choose Apps screen only, Always available, or With chosen apps; choose several apps and keep the tool expanded while any is open. Drag to snap around the center box or any edge. Games still hide tools on their monitor.

Options.Label: Chosen apps (one executable path, name or app ID per line)
Always on (keep the expanded tool visible)
Custom compact format (blank uses the tool's mode)

Control vertical position, 0 to 1 (blank for automatic)

Install and choose which executable names to match in Apps.

Name: Window Opacity
Author: Harbor
Description: Make chosen app windows partly transparent so you can see what is behind them. Some apps manage their own transparency.
Instructions:
Install, then put the target executable names in Apps, one per line.
Set Opacity percent: 100 is solid; 70 lets you see through the window. Click Apply settings.
Open a matching app to try it. Some apps manage their own transparency; the live status below explains skipped effects. Pause restores the original opacity.

Name: Window Title
Author: Harbor
Description: Show the focused app's title as a movable Dock piece.
Instructions:
Enable Window Title in Mods. Optional features start disabled on a new profile.
Show the focused app's title as a movable Dock piece.
Use Customize feature for its controls. Disable it to hide the feature; saved layouts and content are kept.

Name: World Clock
Author: Harbor
Description: See the time in another city without changing your PC’s time zone.
Instructions:
Install, then open Harbor's Apps screen to find the small World time control. Click it to expand the tool; click away or press Esc to collapse.
Set Time zone to a Windows zone name, such as Tokyo Standard Time or Eastern Standard Time.
Choose a time format and click Apply settings.
Right-click the control for Visibility, Position and Appearance. Choose Apps screen only, Always available, or With chosen apps; choose several apps and keep the tool expanded while any is open. Drag to snap around the center box or any edge. Games still hide tools on their monitor.
